docs.title: Quickstart
docs.description: From an empty Next.js + Supabase app to the first agent reply.
docs.body:
Nine steps from an existing Next.js App Router + Supabase app to an AI agent answering “hola” on WhatsApp. Budget under an hour; most of it is the [Meta setup](https://sendo.dev/docs/meta-setup), so open that page in another tab.

> **Note: Before you start**
>
> - Next.js 15+ (App Router), Node 20+, a Supabase project (or `supabase start` locally) and the Supabase CLI.
> - A Meta developer app with the WhatsApp product, a test number and a system user token (see [Meta setup](https://sendo.dev/docs/meta-setup)). If you are starting from zero, Meta’s business verification and app review can take days or weeks; the hour budget starts once you have the app.
> - Everything is public and MIT licensed: no npm or registry token is needed.

## 1. Install the package

`zod` (v4) and `ai` (v6) are peer dependencies, so install them together:

```shell
pnpm add @quami/sendo ai zod
```

## 2. Add the webhook and schema items

Registry items are installed with the standard shadcn CLI from the `@sendo` namespace:

```shell
npx shadcn add @sendo/webhook @sendo/schema
```

- `webhook`: `app/api/sendo/webhook/route.ts` and `lib/sendo.ts` (the client config with TODO hooks). Adds `@supabase/supabase-js`.
- `schema`: the migrations, in order: `supabase/migrations/20261010000000_sendo_v1.sql`, `20261011000000_sendo_v2.sql` (team inbox: snippets, tags, rules) and `20261013000000_sendo_v3.sql` (broadcasts and metrics). Later versions add files; the [changelog](https://sendo.dev/changelog#schema-versions) lists them.

The installed route is three lines:

```ts title="app/api/sendo/webhook/route.ts"
// app/api/sendo/webhook/route.ts (installed by @sendo/webhook)
import { toNextHandlers } from "@quami/sendo/next";
import { sendo } from "@/lib/sendo";

export const { GET, POST } = toNextHandlers(sendo); // POST uses next/server `after()`
export const runtime = "nodejs";
export const maxDuration = 60;
```

If shadcn answers that it doesn't know `@sendo`, add the registry to your `components.json` and run the command again. This is needed only until shadcn's registry index lists `@sendo`; after that the entry is optional.

```json title="components.json"
{
  "registries": {
    "@sendo": "https://registry.sendo.dev/r/{name}.json"
  }
}
```

## 3. Add the inbox

```shell
npx shadcn add @sendo/inbox
```

The staff inbox at `/inbox` (see [Inbox](https://sendo.dev/docs/inbox)). The other screens (numbers, rules, broadcasts, metrics, links) are separate items you add the same way.

## 4. Run the migrations and implement sendo_can_access_tenant

```shell
supabase migration up   # local
supabase db push        # linked project
```

The migrations create the `sendo_*` tables with RLS on every table. The package uses the service role and bypasses RLS; browser clients (the inbox’s realtime subscriptions) only see rows for which `sendo_can_access_tenant(tenant_id)` returns true. It returns `false` by default, so replace it in a migration of your own (keep the signature and the parameter name):

```sql title="supabase/migrations/<ts>_sendo_can_access_tenant.sql"
-- Multi-tenant: a user sees the sendo_* rows of the tenants they belong to.
create or replace function public.sendo_can_access_tenant(tenant_id uuid)
returns boolean language sql stable security definer set search_path = '' as $fn$
  select exists (
    select 1 from public.memberships m
    where m.user_id = auth.uid() and m.tenant_id = sendo_can_access_tenant.tenant_id
  );
$fn$;
```

For a single-tenant app, where every `tenant_id` is null:

```sql title="sql"
-- Single tenant (tenant_id is null): only signed-in staff.
create or replace function public.sendo_can_access_tenant(tenant_id uuid)
returns boolean language sql stable security definer set search_path = '' as $fn$
  select exists (
    select 1 from public.staff s where s.user_id = auth.uid()
  );
$fn$;
```

Inbound media goes to the **private** `sendo-media` Storage bucket. The migration creates it, so there is nothing to run here.

## 5. Set the environment variables

```dotenv title=".env.local"
# Meta app: App settings > Basic > App secret
SENDO_META_APP_SECRET=
# Any random string; paste the same value in the Meta webhook config
SENDO_VERIFY_TOKEN=
# One env var per number; sendo_accounts.token_ref stores this NAME, never the token
SENDO_TOKEN_MAIN=
# Gateway model id (needs AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY) or wire a provider model in lib/sendo.ts
SENDO_AGENT_MODEL=openai/gpt-5-mini
AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY=

# Supabase (server only for the service role key)
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=
SENDO_STORAGE_BUCKET=sendo-media

# Optional: doctor checks this app is subscribed to your WABA
SENDO_META_APP_ID=
```

`SENDO_TOKEN_MAIN` is only a name: each `sendo_accounts` row stores the name of the env var holding its token in `token_ref`, and `resolveToken` reads it at call time. The token is never written to the database or logs. A gateway model id such as `openai/gpt-5-mini` needs AI Gateway credentials; any AI SDK v6 `LanguageModel` works too.

Then fill in the hooks in `lib/sendo.ts` and register an agent. The complete file:

```ts title="lib/sendo.ts"
import { createSendo } from "@quami/sendo";
import { supabaseAdapter } from "@quami/sendo/adapters/supabase";
import { createClient } from "@supabase/supabase-js";
import { z } from "zod";

function requireEnv(name: string): string {
  const value = process.env[name];
  if (value === undefined || value.trim() === "") {
    throw new Error(`[sendo] Missing environment variable ${name}. Add it to .env.local.`);
  }
  return value;
}

// Service-role client: server only, never import this file from client components.
const supabaseAdmin = createClient(
  requireEnv("NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL"),
  requireEnv("SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY"),
  { auth: { persistSession: false, autoRefreshToken: false } },
);

export const sendo = createSendo({
  adapter: supabaseAdapter(supabaseAdmin, {
    storageBucket: process.env.SENDO_STORAGE_BUCKET ?? "sendo-media",
  }),
  appSecret: requireEnv("SENDO_META_APP_SECRET"),
  verifyToken: requireEnv("SENDO_VERIFY_TOKEN"),
  // sendo_accounts.token_ref holds the NAME of the env var with the token (e.g. SENDO_TOKEN_MAIN).
  resolveToken: (account) => process.env[account.tokenRef],
  // findPatientIdByPhone / listAdminIds stand for your own queries.
  // Your entity id for this phone number (patient, resident, user), or null.
  linkContact: async ({ phone, account }) => findPatientIdByPhone(phone, account.tenantId),
  // Who gets a handed-off conversation. Exactly one id auto-assigns it.
  resolveHandoffTargets: async ({ account }) => listAdminIds(account.tenantId),
  agentDefaults: { historyLimit: 20, maxStepsPerTurn: 5, maxMessagesPerMinutePerContact: 10 },
  eventRetentionDays: 30,
  logger: console,
});
```

Append the agent to the same file:

```ts title="lib/sendo.ts (continued)"
sendo.agent({
  name: "recepcion",
  model: requireEnv("SENDO_AGENT_MODEL"), // e.g. "openai/gpt-5-mini" via the AI Gateway
  instructions: "Eres la recepcionista de la clínica. Responde breve y en español.",
  tools: {
    horarios: {
      description: "Horarios de atención de la clínica",
      input: z.object({}),
      run: async () => ({ lunesAViernes: "08:00-17:00", sabado: "08:00-12:00" }),
    },
  },
  handoff: { when: "El paciente pide hablar con una persona", to: "recepcion" },
  fallbackMessage: "Tuvimos un problema. Una persona del equipo te responderá pronto.",
});
```

## 6. Register the number in sendo_accounts

```shell
npx @quami/sendo accounts add --phone-number-id 123456789012345 --token-env SENDO_TOKEN_MAIN
```

It reads `.env.local`, refuses to run when the token variable is empty, fetches the display phone and (when possible) the WABA id from Meta, and stores only the variable name. Flags and prompts: [CLI](https://sendo.dev/docs/cli#accounts-add). Or insert the row yourself:

```sql title="sql"
-- Alternative to `npx @quami/sendo accounts add`. token_ref is the env var NAME.
insert into public.sendo_accounts (tenant_id, phone_number_id, waba_id, display_phone, token_ref)
values (null, '123456789012345', '987654321098765', '+1 555 000 1111', 'SENDO_TOKEN_MAIN');
```

## 7. Point the Meta webhook at your app

In the Meta App Dashboard, **WhatsApp › Configuration**: set the Callback URL to `https://<app>/api/sendo/webhook` and the Verify token to the value of `SENDO_VERIFY_TOKEN`, click **Verify and save**, then subscribe the `messages` webhook field. In development, expose your dev server with a tunnel ([ngrok or cloudflared](https://sendo.dev/docs/meta-setup#tunnel)).

## 8. Run doctor

```shell
npx @quami/sendo doctor --url https://<app>/api/sendo/webhook
```

Every check should pass: env vars, tables and schema version, the storage bucket, each account’s token and phone status, the WABA subscription, template listing and the webhook verify round-trip. Each failure prints a fix hint and the command exits with code 1. See [all checks](https://sendo.dev/docs/cli#doctor).

## 9. Send “hola”

From a phone added as a test recipient, send `hola` to the test number. The webhook returns 200 immediately, stores the message, and the `recepcion` agent answers within seconds. Ask for a person to see the handoff: the conversation moves to `human` and shows up in the inbox.

> **Warning: No reply?**
>
> - Run `doctor` again and check your server logs for `[sendo]` lines.
> - Look at `sendo_events`: `unrouted` means the `phone_number_id` isn’t in `sendo_accounts`; `failed` carries the error. Fix it and call `sendo.events.reprocess(id)`.
> - Nothing in `sendo_events`: the webhook isn’t reaching you (URL, tunnel, `messages` subscription) or the signature fails (wrong `SENDO_META_APP_SECRET`, 401).

Next: [API reference](https://sendo.dev/docs/api-reference), [Security](https://sendo.dev/docs/security) and [Retention](https://sendo.dev/docs/retention).

docs.title: Meta setup
docs.description: App, WhatsApp product, test number, system user token and webhook.
docs.body:
Sendo only talks to the official WhatsApp Cloud API. You need a Meta Business account (business.facebook.com) and a developer account (developers.facebook.com). Meta renames menu items from time to time; the names below match the dashboard at the time of writing.

## 1. Create the Meta app

1. developers.facebook.com › **My Apps** › **Create app**.
2. Choose the **Business** type (or the “Connect with customers through WhatsApp” use case) and link it to your Meta Business account.

## 2. Add the WhatsApp product

In the app dashboard, **Add product** › **WhatsApp** › **Set up**. Meta creates a WhatsApp Business Account (WABA) for the business and opens **WhatsApp › API Setup**.

## 3. Test number and recipients

- API Setup shows a free **test number** with its **Phone number ID** and the **WhatsApp Business Account ID**. Copy both.
- Under **To**, add up to five recipient numbers and verify them with the code Meta sends. The test number can only message verified recipients.
- For production, add your own number under **WhatsApp › API Setup › Add phone number** (it must not be registered in the WhatsApp app) and complete the display name review.

## 4. System user token

The temporary token on API Setup expires after 24 hours. Use a system user token, which doesn’t expire:

1. business.facebook.com › **Settings** › **Users › System users** › **Add** (role Admin).
2. **Assign assets**: your app, and the WhatsApp account with full control.
3. **Generate token**: pick the app, expiration **Never**, and the permissions `whatsapp_business_messaging` and `whatsapp_business_management`.
4. Put it in an env var such as `SENDO_TOKEN_MAIN` (locally and in your deployment). Never commit it and never store it in the database.

> **Warning:**
>
> `whatsapp_business_management` is required for template sync and for `doctor`’s subscription and template checks. A revoked or expired token surfaces as `MetaApiError` with `metaCode` 190, fires the `account.error` event, and fails `doctor`.

## 5. App secret

App dashboard › **App settings › Basic** › **App secret** › Show. This is `SENDO_META_APP_SECRET`: Sendo verifies the `X-Hub-Signature-256` HMAC of every webhook POST with it and answers 401 on a mismatch. The **App ID** on the same page is the optional `SENDO_META_APP_ID` that `doctor` uses to confirm the app is subscribed to your WABA.

## 6. Tunnel for local development

Meta must reach your webhook over public HTTPS. Start the dev server, then one of:

```shell
ngrok http 3000
# or
cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:3000
```

Use the printed `https://…` host as the callback URL. Free ngrok and quick cloudflared tunnels change host on every start, so update the callback URL (and rerun `doctor --url`) when they do.

## 7. Webhook and the messages field

1. Pick a random verify token and set it as `SENDO_VERIFY_TOKEN`, e.g. `openssl rand -hex 24`. Restart the dev server.
2. App dashboard › **WhatsApp › Configuration** › Webhook › **Edit**: Callback URL `https://<host>/api/sendo/webhook`, Verify token = `SENDO_VERIFY_TOKEN`, **Verify and save**. Meta sends a GET challenge; Sendo answers it only when the token matches (403 otherwise).
3. Under **Webhook fields**, **Subscribe** to `messages`. It carries inbound messages and the sent / delivered / read / failed statuses. For numbers shared with the WhatsApp Business app, also subscribe to `smb_message_echoes`, `history` and `smb_app_state_sync` ([Coexistence](https://sendo.dev/docs/coexistence)).
4. If `doctor` reports the app isn’t subscribed to the WABA, subscribe it with the token:

```shell
curl -X POST "https://graph.facebook.com/v26.0/<WABA_ID>/subscribed_apps" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SENDO_TOKEN_MAIN"
```

## Where each value goes

| Meta value                   | sendo                                                                             |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Phone number ID              | `sendo_accounts.phone_number_id` (`--phone-number-id`); webhooks are routed by it |
| WhatsApp Business Account ID | `sendo_accounts.waba_id` (`--waba-id`, auto-detected when possible)               |
| System user token            | env var named by `sendo_accounts.token_ref` (`--token-env`)                       |
| App secret                   | `SENDO_META_APP_SECRET`                                                           |
| Verify token (yours)         | `SENDO_VERIFY_TOKEN`                                                              |
| App ID (optional)            | `SENDO_META_APP_ID`                                                               |

Back to [Quickstart step 6](https://sendo.dev/docs/quickstart#account).

docs.title: Meta pricing
docs.description: Who pays Meta for WhatsApp messages, where to find the official rates, and why a payment method matters.

headings.title: A payment method on every account

docs.body:
Sendo moves no money. **Meta bills the owner of the WhatsApp Business account** (the building, the clinic, your customer) directly, per delivered message. Sendo and Quami never re-bill messages. This page links to Meta’s official information and never copies rates, which change by country, category and date.

## Official sources

- [WhatsApp Business Platform pricing](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/pricing): how messages are billed, categories, free entry points, announced changes and the rate cards per country.
- [Meta Business Suite billing](https://business.facebook.com/billing_hub): where the account owner adds a payment method and sees invoices.

## How billing works, in short

- Since July 2025, Meta bills **per delivered message**, priced by the recipient’s country and the template category (marketing, utility, authentication).
- Replies inside the 24-hour customer service window are service messages. Meta has announced that from **October 1, 2026** service messages above 1,000 free per number per month are billed at the utility rate; confirm the current rule on the pricing page above.
- Instagram and Messenger messages are not billed per message.

## A payment method on every account

The account owner must add a payment method in Meta. Until they do, sends fail with Meta error 131042. Sendo tracks this as `billingReady` on each number: the numbers screen shows “falta método de pago”, sends throw with the `billing_not_ready` hint, `sendo doctor` warns, and broadcasts pause until it is fixed. See [Embedded Signup](https://sendo.dev/docs/embedded-signup#billing).

## Estimating your costs

Count the templates you send per month by category and destination country, multiply by Meta’s current rate card, and add the service messages above the free tier. [Metrics](https://sendo.dev/docs/metrics) gives you message counts per day to check the estimate against Meta’s invoices.

docs.title: Sendo Connect
docs.description: The optional paid service: Quami as your Meta Tech Provider. Configuration, the signed webhook relay, signup through Connect, doctor checks and what passes through Quami.
docs.body:
Sendo is free and MIT licensed. The only paid piece is **Sendo Connect**: Quami acts as the Meta **Tech Provider** for your app, so you can offer “Connect your WhatsApp” without going through Meta’s business verification and app review yourself. Price: **precio por confirmar** (per connected number, per month; see [Pricing](https://sendo.dev/pricing)).

> **Warning: The service is opening**
>
> The package side below ships in `@quami/sendo`. Connect accounts (API key, signing secret, panel) open when Quami’s Tech Provider verification is approved; until then, use [your own Meta app](https://sendo.dev/docs/meta-setup).

## What changes with Connect

- **Configuration only.** The package, the migrations and the registry components are identical; you add `connect: { apiKey, signingSecret }` to `createSendo`.
- **Signup** goes through Quami’s Meta app: the number’s token is returned to your server once and never stored by Connect.
- **Webhooks** arrive through Quami’s relay, signed with your own secret (`X-Sendo-Signature`), and are verified fail-closed by your app.
- **Sending** still goes directly from your server to Meta with the customer’s token.

## Setup

1. In the Connect panel, create a project and copy the **API key** and the **signing secret** into `SENDO_CONNECT_API_KEY` and `SENDO_CONNECT_SIGNING_SECRET` (`.env.local` and your deployment).
2. Register your webhook URL in the panel: `https://<your-domain>/api/sendo/webhook` (the `webhook` route). You don’t configure a webhook in Meta.
3. In `lib/sendo.ts`, remove `appSecret` and add `connect`. Set `meta.appId` / `configId` (and `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENDO_META_APP_ID` / `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENDO_META_CONFIG_ID` for the connect button) to Quami’s values from the panel.
4. Run `npx @quami/sendo doctor --url https://<your-domain>/api/sendo/webhook` ([checks below](#doctor)).

```ts title="lib/sendo.ts"
export const sendo = createSendo({
  adapter: memoryAdapter(), // your adapter
  // No appSecret: with `connect`, webhooks are verified with X-Sendo-Signature only.
  verifyToken: process.env.SENDO_VERIFY_TOKEN ?? "",
  resolveToken: (account) => readSecret(account.tokenRef),
  storeToken, // Embedded Signup tokens still go to your secret store
  connect: {
    apiKey: process.env.SENDO_CONNECT_API_KEY ?? "",
    signingSecret: process.env.SENDO_CONNECT_SIGNING_SECRET ?? "",
  },
});
```

`baseUrl` defaults to `https://connect.sendo.dev`. `apiKey` and `signingSecret` are registered as secrets: the logger and errors redact them like tokens.

## Webhook signature

With `connect` set, `sendo.handleWebhook` (and `toNextHandlers`) accepts a `POST` only when `X-Sendo-Signature` is valid:

```
X-Sendo-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex hmac_sha256(signingSecret, t + "." + rawBody)>
```

- The timestamp must be within **5 minutes** of your server’s clock (either direction), so a captured request can’t be replayed later. Keep the server clock synced.
- The comparison is constant-time. Several `v1=` values are allowed (any may match) so the secret can be rotated.
- Anything else (missing, malformed, stale, wrong secret, body changed) is `401` and nothing is stored.
- **Meta’s `X-Hub-Signature-256` is not accepted** while `connect` is set, even if `appSecret` is still configured. Without `connect`, nothing changes: Meta’s signature is the only one checked.

To try your route locally, sign a fixture the way the relay does with `signConnectBody` (and `verifyConnectSignature` checks one):

```ts title="ts"
// Sign a body the way the relay does, to try your webhook route locally.
export function relayHeaders(rawBody: string): Record<string, string> {
  return {
    "content-type": "application/json",
    "x-sendo-signature": signConnectBody(rawBody, process.env.SENDO_CONNECT_SIGNING_SECRET ?? ""),
  };
}
```

## Signup through Connect

`sendo.accounts.completeEmbeddedSignup(input)` takes the same input and returns the same `Account`. With `connect`, steps 1–4 of the [direct sequence](https://sendo.dev/docs/embedded-signup#sequence) are one call to Connect:

```
POST {baseUrl}/v1/signup/complete
Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>
{ "code", "wabaId", "phoneNumberId", "coexistence", "pin" }   →   200 { "token", "displayPhone" }
```

`pin` is the admin’s PIN or a random 6 digits (`null` for coexistence numbers, which skip `register`). Then Sendo continues exactly as in the direct path: `storeToken`, insert or reconnect the account (`onboardedVia: "connect"`), first number becomes the default, billing check. A failure after `storeToken` compensates the same way (no row left, `deleteToken`, app unsubscribed).

Errors keep the same codes. Connect reports Meta failures as `{ "error": { "code", "message", "step", "metaCode", "subcode", "fbtraceId" } }`, which map to `SIGNUP_CODE_EXPIRED`, `META_PERMISSION_MISSING`, `PIN_CONFLICT` or `SIGNUP_FAILED` with that `step`. A rejected API key (401) is `CONFIG_ERROR` naming `SENDO_CONNECT_API_KEY`; Connect unreachable or an answer without a token is `SIGNUP_FAILED` with `step: "connect"`. `meta.appId` and `appSecret` are not needed on your side.

## Doctor checks

When `SENDO_CONNECT_API_KEY` or `SENDO_CONNECT_SIGNING_SECRET` is set, `sendo doctor` requires both (and no longer requires `SENDO_META_APP_SECRET`) and calls `GET {baseUrl}/v1/projects/current/webhook` (`SENDO_CONNECT_BASE_URL` overrides the base URL):

| Check              | Fails when                                                                                                                         | Fix                                                                         |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `connect:key`      | Connect rejects the key, or can’t be reached                                                                                       | Copy the current key from the panel; check `SENDO_CONNECT_BASE_URL`         |
| `connect:webhook`  | No URL registered, or a different one from `--url`                                                                                 | Register `https://<your-domain>/api/sendo/webhook` in the panel             |
| `connect:delivery` | The relay’s last delivery got a non-2xx answer (401 = signing secret mismatch or clock skew); warns when nothing was delivered yet | Fix `SENDO_CONNECT_SIGNING_SECRET` or the route; the relay retries for 24 h |

## What stays the same

- Meta bills message costs to your customer’s WhatsApp Business account, not to Quami ([Meta pricing](https://sendo.dev/docs/meta-pricing)). Connect is billed per connected number.
- Before charging, Connect shows the billing caveat: “Meta cobra los mensajes directo a tu cliente; necesita tarjeta en su cuenta.” Until the customer adds a card, sends fail with 131042 and the number shows “falta método de pago” ([billing](https://sendo.dev/docs/embedded-signup#billing)).
- Your data stays in your database.

## Privacy

Messages pass through Quami’s relay in transit and are never stored or logged there; only delivery metadata (ids, timestamps, status codes) is kept, for 7 days. Apps with sensitive data (health, for example) should use **their own Meta app** instead.

## Doing it yourself

Being your own Tech Provider stays a first-class, free path: see [Meta setup](https://sendo.dev/docs/meta-setup) and [Embedded Signup](https://sendo.dev/docs/embedded-signup).

docs.title: API reference
docs.description: Config, events, sending, templates, conversations, agents and adapters.

docs.title: Agents and models
docs.description: Give an agent any AI SDK model: OpenRouter or a gateway for exploring, a direct provider for production, and what each turn costs.

headings.title: For exploring: one key, many models

docs.body:
An agent’s `model` is any AI SDK v6 `LanguageModel`, or a gateway model id string. Sendo never picks a provider for you and has no model bundled.

```ts
import { openai } from "@ai-sdk/openai";

sendo.agent({
  name: "recepcion",
  model: openai("gpt-5-mini"), // or "openai/gpt-5-mini" through the AI Gateway
  instructions: "Eres la recepcionista de la clínica. Responde breve y en español.",
  pricing: { inputPerMTok: 0.25, outputPerMTok: 2 }, // optional, USD; used for costCents
});
```

The full definition (tools, handoff, draft mode, limits) is in the [API reference](https://sendo.dev/docs/api-reference#agents).

## For exploring: one key, many models

**OpenRouter** (through its AI SDK provider) or the **Vercel AI Gateway** (a string id such as `"openai/gpt-5-mini"`) let you try many models with one key and switch by changing a string. That is the fastest way to find a model that is good and cheap enough for your conversations.

Two costs to know about:

- **A markup.** These services add a fee on top of the provider’s price. Check their current pricing pages; Sendo doesn’t copy rates.
- **An extra network hop.** Every turn goes through one more service, which adds latency and one more thing that can fail.

## For production: a direct provider

Once you know the model, call its provider directly (`@ai-sdk/openai`, `@ai-sdk/anthropic`, `@ai-sdk/google`, …): no markup, one hop fewer, and the provider’s own data terms. For sensitive data (health, finance), read those terms and prefer providers with zero data retention agreements.

Changing the model is one line in `lib/sendo.ts`; nothing else in Sendo depends on it.

## What a turn costs

Every agent turn stores `tokensIn` and `tokensOut` on the reply (or draft) message, and `costCents`:

1. the provider’s reported cost when it gives one (OpenRouter reports it per call);
2. otherwise `pricing` from the agent definition (USD per million input and output tokens);
3. otherwise `null`, shown as “—”.

Admins see the cost of each turn in the inbox; [Metrics](https://sendo.dev/docs/metrics) adds cost per day and per agent. See [Voice notes and cost](https://sendo.dev/docs/voice-notes-and-cost).

## Keep turns bounded

- `historyLimit` (default 20 messages) bounds what the model reads.
- `maxStepsPerTurn` (default 5) bounds tool calls per turn.
- `maxMessagesPerMinutePerContact` (default 10) skips turns for floods; messages are still stored.
- To cap output tokens, wrap the model with the AI SDK’s `wrapLanguageModel` and a middleware that sets `maxOutputTokens` (the [live demo](https://sendo.dev/demo) caps every call at 300 this way).

## One agent for many organizations

`tenants` and `accounts` restrict where an agent answers, and `instructions` can be a function of the account’s tenant. See [Numbers and tenants](https://sendo.dev/docs/numbers-and-tenants#agents).

docs.title: Security
docs.description: Sensitive data, private storage, signed URLs, tokens and authorization inside tools.
docs.body:
## Where data lives

Sendo has no server of its own. Messages, contacts, media and raw webhooks are stored only in your Supabase project (`sendo_*` tables and your Storage bucket), behind your RLS. Quami never receives them. For sensitive data (health, finance, minors) that means your app is the data controller for WhatsApp content too: apply the same policies you apply to the rest of your records.

## Private bucket and signed URLs

- Inbound media is downloaded from Meta right away (Meta’s URLs expire in minutes) and stored at `{tenant_id | _}/{account_id}/{conversation_id}/{meta_media_id}.{ext}` in `SENDO_STORAGE_BUCKET`.
- The bucket **must be private** (`public = false`). `doctor` checks that it exists, not its visibility, so check it in Supabase Studio.
- The inbox only shows media through signed URLs valid for 300 seconds (`sendo.inbox.thread`). Don’t persist signed URLs or make objects public to “fix” previews.
- Don’t add Storage policies that let browser clients read the bucket directly.

## Retention and encryption are yours

Sendo prunes only `sendo_events` (raw webhook payloads, 30 days by default). It never deletes `sendo_messages` or `sendo_media`, and it doesn’t encrypt message content:

- Decide how long conversations and files are kept and delete them on a schedule (see the example in [Retention](https://sendo.dev/docs/retention#messages-media)).
- Encryption at rest is your database’s and storage provider’s (Supabase encrypts disks and backups). If you need column-level encryption, add it in your app; note that `sendo_messages.text` holds a plain-text copy of the body for previews and search.
- Raw payloads in `sendo_events.payload` contain message text and phone numbers; keep `eventRetentionDays` as short as your reprocessing needs allow.

## Authorization inside tools

The agent’s context is limited to one contact and one conversation, and tool input is validated with zod before `run`. That doesn’t make the input trustworthy: a user can write anything, including instructions aimed at the model (prompt injection). So:

- Authorize in `run` from the context Sendo gives you (`contact.appRef`, `account.tenantId`), never from ids the model passes in.
- Handle `contact.appRef === null` (unlinked contacts): ask for an identifier and verify it, don’t guess.
- Return only what this contact may see. Tool results go back to the model.
- Give tools the narrowest scope: read-only where possible, no generic SQL.

```ts title="ts"
const agendarCita = agentTool({
  description: "Agenda una cita para el paciente vinculado a esta conversación",
  input: z.object({ fecha: z.iso.date(), hora: z.string().regex(/^\d{2}:\d{2}$/) }),
  // `input` is already validated (and typed) by the zod schema.
  async run({ input, contact, account }) {
    // Authorize inside the tool: only act on the entity linked to THIS contact.
    if (contact.appRef === null) {
      return { error: "Paciente no identificado. Pide su número de DPI." };
    }
    return bookAppointment({
      tenantId: account.tenantId,
      patientId: contact.appRef,
      date: input.fecha,
      time: input.hora,
    });
  },
});
```

## Tokens and secrets

- `sendo_accounts.token_ref` stores the **name** of an env var or secret. Tokens are resolved per call through `resolveToken(account)` and never written to the database.
- Logs are redacted: the logger strips `Authorization` headers, `access_token` parameters, the app secret, the verify token and every token it resolved. `MetaApiError` messages are redacted too, and `toJSON()` omits `cause` and `stack`. `doctor` never prints a token.
- `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` bypasses RLS: server only, never in a `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` variable.

> **Important:**
>
> A token pasted into `sendo_accounts.token_ref` is a leaked token. Rotate it in Meta Business Settings and store the variable name instead.

## Webhook verification

POSTs are checked with HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body against `X-Hub-Signature-256` using your app secret, compared in constant time; a bad signature returns 401 and stores nothing. The GET verify token is also compared in constant time.

## Database access

RLS is enabled on every `sendo_*` table, with only SELECT policies through `sendo_can_access_tenant(tenant_id)` (default `false`). Events, locks and schema metadata are service-role only, and browser clients can’t write. Keep it that way: writes go through server actions that call your auth check ([Inbox](https://sendo.dev/docs/inbox#auth)).

headings.title: What already works for every channel
Why not ship links for channels that don't exist yet

docs.body:
Sendo ships one channel: **WhatsApp** (Cloud API). Instagram and Messenger are not built yet. The schema, the webhook and the parser layout are already shaped for them, so adding them later is new code in the package, not a migration in your app.

## What already works for every channel

- **Schema.** `sendo_accounts`, `sendo_contacts` and `sendo_conversations` carry a `channel` column, and contacts are identified by `channel_user_id` (the phone is optional). Schema v1 was rewritten with this before the first release, so a new channel needs no migration.
- **Webhook dispatch.** `sendo.handleWebhook` verifies `X-Hub-Signature-256` once for every Meta product, stores the event, and dispatches on the body’s `object` to that channel’s parser (`whatsapp_business_account` today).
- **Unknown products are kept, not lost.** A body for `instagram` or `page` before those channels exist is stored as an `unrouted` event (`event.unrouted`) and answered with 200, so Meta doesn’t retry forever. You can reprocess it later with `sendo.events.reprocess(id)`.
- **The inbox, team features, rules and metrics** read the `channel` of each conversation; the list shows a channel badge on the avatar.

## What changes per channel

|                                | WhatsApp                                                                                            | Instagram / Messenger (later)                  |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| Contact id                     | Phone (`wa_id`) and `channel_user_id`                                                               | Page-scoped id only (no phone)                 |
| Starting a conversation        | Approved templates outside the 24-hour window                                                       | Meta’s messaging-window rules for each product |
| Links                          | `wa.me` links and QR ([Widgets](https://sendo.dev/docs/widgets))                                                     | `ig.me` / `m.me`, added when the channel ships |
| Billing                        | Meta bills the WhatsApp Business account per delivered message ([Meta pricing](https://sendo.dev/docs/meta-pricing)) | Not billed per message                         |
| Coexistence with the phone app | [Coexistence](https://sendo.dev/docs/coexistence)                                                                    | Not applicable                                 |

## One person, several channels

A person who writes on WhatsApp and later on Instagram becomes **two contacts and two conversations**, joined by the same `app_ref` (the record in your app that `linkContact` returns). Merging them into one thread is a UI decision left for later; your app already knows they are the same customer.

## Why not ship links for channels that don't exist yet

The link generator (`sendo.links.create`) and the chat bubble are WhatsApp-only on purpose: a link to a channel whose messages Sendo can’t receive would be a broken promise.

docs.body:
Coexistence lets a business keep the WhatsApp Business app on its phone while the same number works through the Cloud API, so the owner answers from the phone and the team (and the AI) answers from your inbox. Sendo stores what the owner sends from the phone, pauses the AI where the owner stepped in and, if you want, imports the phone’s chat history.

> **Warning:**
>
> Coexistence has changed several times at Meta. The requirements and limits below were checked against Meta’s documentation on October 9, 2026 and are re-verified during the real-Meta smoke run. Nothing about coexistence goes on the landing page until Meta confirms them.

## Meta’s requirements

- The number is onboarded through **Embedded Signup** with the WhatsApp Business app flavour (`featureType: "whatsapp_business_app_onboarding"`, `sessionInfoVersion: "3"` or later). The older `coexistence` value is deprecated, and Embedded Signup v2 is retired around October 15, 2026.
- You are a Meta **Solution Partner or Tech Provider**, with Embedded Signup session logging on (see [Embedded Signup](https://sendo.dev/docs/embedded-signup)).
- The business uses WhatsApp Business app **2.24.17 or later**.
- Your app subscribes to three extra **webhook fields**: `smb_message_echoes`, `history` and `smb_app_state_sync` (next to `messages`).
- Sendo doesn’t call `register` for a coexistence number (the phone app keeps it registered), and the account is stored with `coexistence = true`.

## Limits

- **Throughput:** a number used on both the app and the Cloud API is capped at 20 messages per second.
- **24-hour window:** only messages received after onboarding open it. Messages sent from the phone app are free and don’t open or extend the window.
- **History:** contacts and history can each be synced once, within 24 hours of onboarding, for up to 180 days back. Group chats are not included. Media in history arrives later and only for the last 14 days.
- **Not available through the Cloud API:** group chats, disappearing and view-once messages, live location, broadcast lists (existing ones become read-only), voice and video calls, catalogs/orders/status, quick replies, labels, greeting and away messages, business profile settings and Channels.
- **Companion devices:** up to four; onboarding unlinks the existing ones (WhatsApp for Windows and Wear OS aren’t supported).
- The number can’t be deregistered through the API while it is shared; the business disconnects it from the app.

## What Sendo does

| Webhook field        | Sendo                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `smb_message_echoes` | Each message the owner sent from the phone is stored as an outbound message: sender `human`, `senderRef: "business_app"`, `metadata.origin: "business_app"`, status `sent`, its Meta id. The inbox shows it as "Desde el teléfono". A repeated echo is stored once.          |
| `history`            | With `importHistory`, each message is stored with `metadata.imported = true` (the owner’s with `senderRef: "business_app"`). Imported messages never count as unread, never open the window and never start an AI turn. Without it, the webhook is acknowledged and ignored. |
| `smb_app_state_sync` | Acknowledged (contact sync isn’t stored yet). Subscribe anyway: Meta requires it for coexistence.                                                                                                                                                                            |

An echo updates the conversation’s last activity and clears “awaiting reply”, but never `last_inbound_at` or the window. It creates the contact and conversation if the owner started the chat from the phone. It doesn’t fire the `message` event (that one is for inbound messages).

### The AI steps aside

When the owner answers from the phone in a conversation the AI is handling (status `agent`), Sendo pauses the AI **on that conversation** so the owner and the AI never double-answer. It emits `conversation.agent_paused` with `by: "business_app"`. Later inbound messages are stored, count as unread and keep the window open, but the AI runs no turns until the conversation is resumed from the inbox. Turn it off with `pauseAgentOnPhoneReply: false`.

A reply the AI was already writing when the echo arrived may still go out. This is a known limit: the pause stops the next turn, not one in flight.

```ts title="ts"
sendo.on("conversation.agent_paused", ({ conversation, paused, by }) => {
  if (by === "business_app" && paused) {
    console.log(`The owner answered ${conversation.id} from the phone; the AI is paused there.`);
  }
});
```

## Config

| Option                               | Default | Notes                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------ | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `coexistence.pauseAgentOnPhoneReply` | `true`  | Pause the AI on a conversation when the owner replies from the phone app. |
| `coexistence.importHistory`          | `false` | Store `history` webhooks as imported messages.                            |

```ts title="ts"
export const sendo = createSendo({
  adapter: memoryAdapter(),
  appSecret: process.env.SENDO_META_APP_SECRET ?? "",
  verifyToken: process.env.SENDO_VERIFY_TOKEN ?? "",
  resolveToken: (account) => process.env[account.tokenRef],
  coexistence: {
    // An owner's reply from the phone pauses the AI on that conversation (default true).
    pauseAgentOnPhoneReply: true,
    // Store the phone app's chat history when Meta sends it (default false).
    importHistory: true,
  },
});
```

## Known gaps

- Imported messages keep Meta’s timestamp in `sent_at` (incoming) but are ordered in the thread by when Sendo stored them.
- Media inside echoes is downloaded like inbound media; media inside history is not (Meta sends it separately and only for 14 days).
- Edits and revokes made from the phone aren’t applied to stored messages yet.

headings.title: Why not Instagram or Messenger links yet

docs.body: A conversation that starts from a sign at the gate, a link on an invoice or a button on your website should say so. Sendo builds a WhatsApp click-to-chat link whose prefilled message ends with a short visible code, like `[#garita]`. When a contact sends that message, the new conversation is tagged with the source, and you can count conversations per source. ## Create a link `sendo.links.create({ account?, tenant?, text?, source })` returns `{ url, code, phone, text }`. It picks the number the same way `send.*` does (an explicit `account`, else the tenant’s default number), reads it, and writes nothing. ```ts title="ts" // The tenant's default number (or pass `account`: its id or Meta phone number id). const link = await sendo.links.create({ tenant: tenantId, text: "Hola, quiero información", source: "garita", }); // link.url → "https://wa.me/50255551234?text=Hola%2C%20quiero%20informaci%C3%B3n%20%5B%23garita%5D" // link.text → "Hola, quiero información [#garita]" // link.code → "[#garita]" // link.phone → "+50255551234" ``` - `source` must match `^[a-z0-9-]{1,32}$` (lowercase letters, digits and `-`). Anything else throws `INVALID_PAYLOAD`. - The URL is `https://wa.me/?text=`, percent-encoded. Without `text` the message is just the code. - The contact can edit the message before sending it. If they delete the code, the conversation is simply “direct”. When you already know the number, `buildWhatsAppLink` builds the same link with no lookup: ```ts title="ts" // No lookup at all when you already know the number. const direct = buildWhatsAppLink({ phone: "+502 5555 1234", text: "Hola", source: "factura" }); ``` ## How attribution works - The pipeline reads a trailing `[#code]` from the **first inbound message of a new or reopened conversation** only. It sets `conversation.source` and `message.metadata.source`. A code in a later message is ignored. - The stored message keeps the full text. The AI agent gets the text without the code, and the inbox shows it without the code plus an “Origen: garita” chip. - A Click-to-WhatsApp ad sets `source = "ad:"` from Meta’s `referral`. With neither, `source` is `null` (direct). ## Count conversations per source ```ts title="ts" // Admin only (`numbers.manage`); scoped to the actor's tenant. `source: null` = direct. const sources = await sendo.links.sources({ actor: admin, from: new Date("2026-10-01") }); // [{ source: "garita", conversations: 42 }, { source: null, conversations: 17 }, ...] ``` Sorted by count, most first, ties by name, `null` (direct) last among equals. It needs an actor with `numbers.manage` (admins, see the roles table in the inbox docs) and throws `FORBIDDEN` otherwise. Pass `account` to count a single number, and `from` / `to` to limit by when the conversation was created. ## The `widgets` registry item ```shell npx shadcn add @sendo/widgets ``` It adds: - **The “Enlaces” screen** at `/inbox/links` (`app/(protected)/inbox/links`): pick a number, write the message and the source, then copy the link, download the QR as PNG or SVG, and copy the chat bubble snippet. Below it, the sources table with conversation counts. Admins only. - **``** (`components/sendo/widgets/qr-code.tsx`): error correction H (Q when the message makes the code too dense, never lower), a 4-module quiet zone, always black on white so phones read it in dark mode too. The PNG and SVG are generated in the browser; no external QR service sees your links. It uses `qrcode-generator`, a dependency of the item, not of `@quami/sendo`. - **``** (`components/sendo/widgets/chat-bubble.tsx`) for your public site. Before using the screen, implement `requireUser()` in `app/(protected)/inbox/links/links-config.ts` (it throws until you do) and configure `resolveRole` in `createSendo`. ## Chat bubble A floating button that opens WhatsApp with the message ready. It’s a plain link, so it works in Server and Client Components and needs no client JavaScript. It has hover and press states, and with `prefers-reduced-motion` the press doesn’t scale. ```tsx title="app/layout.tsx" import { SendoChatBubble } from "@/components/sendo/widgets/chat-bubble"; export default function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) { return ( {children} ); } ``` | Prop | Type | Notes | | ---------- | --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `phone` | `string` | Any format; only the digits are used. Renders nothing when it isn’t 7–15 digits. | | `text` | `string?` | Prefilled message. | | `source` | `string?` | Appended as `[#source]`. | | `href` | `string?` | A link from `sendo.links.create` (overrides `phone`, `text`, `source`). | | `position` | `"bottom-right" \| "bottom-left"` | Default `bottom-right`. | | `label` | `string?` | Accessible name and tooltip. Default “Escríbenos por WhatsApp”. | To pick the number by account or tenant instead of by phone, build the link on the server and pass `href={link.url}`. ## Without React The bubble is a convenience. Any site, email or PDF can use the plain link, and attribution works the same: ```html Escríbenos por WhatsApp ``` Encode the whole message with `encodeURIComponent` (`[` is `%5B`, `#` is `%23`, `]` is `%5D`). There is no non-React embed script for the bubble. ## Why not Instagram or Messenger links yet Instagram (`ig.me`) and Messenger (`m.me`) have their own click-to-chat links, and Sendo’s schema already has a `channel` column for them. But only WhatsApp messages are parsed and answered today. A link to a channel whose messages never reach your inbox would be a broken promise, so the link builder is WhatsApp-only and will add `ig.me` / `m.me` when those channels ship.

docs.title: CLI
docs.description: npx @quami/sendo doctor, accounts add, list, set-default and disconnect, and rules sync: checks, flags and environment.
docs.body:
The package ships a `sendo` binary. Run it from your app’s root with `npx @quami/sendo <command>` (or `npx sendo` once installed). Output, prompts and errors are in English; `--help` lists every flag.

```shell title="usage"
sendo doctor [--account <id>] [--url <url>] [--json] [--config <path>]
sendo accounts add [--phone-number-id <id>] [--waba-id <id>] [--token-env <VAR>]
                   [--tenant-id <uuid>] [--display-phone <number>] [--timezone <IANA>] [--yes]
sendo accounts list [--tenant-id <uuid>] [--json]
sendo accounts set-default <id>
sendo accounts disconnect <id>
sendo rules sync --config <path> [--force] [--tenant <id>]
sendo mcp [--config <path>]
sendo --help | --version
```

## Environment

Both commands load `.env.development.local`, `.env.local` and `.env` from the current directory, in that order, without overriding variables already set in the shell. To check production values, export them or run the command where they are defined.

| Variable                                                | Used for                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SENDO_META_APP_SECRET`                                 | Required (env check), unless the Connect variables are set.                              |
| `SENDO_VERIFY_TOKEN`                                    | Required; also used for the --url challenge.                                             |
| `SUPABASE_URL or NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`              | Supabase project URL.                                                                    |
| `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`                             | Reads sendo_accounts, schema and storage; accounts add inserts with it.                  |
| `SENDO_STORAGE_BUCKET`                                  | Bucket to check. Default sendo-media.                                                    |
| `<token_ref>`                                           | One per account, e.g. SENDO_TOKEN_MAIN. Must be set locally for doctor and accounts add. |
| `SENDO_META_APP_ID`                                     | Optional. When set, doctor also checks this app is in the WABA's subscribed apps.        |
| `SENDO_CONNECT_API_KEY`, `SENDO_CONNECT_SIGNING_SECRET` | Sendo Connect: when either is set both are required and the `connect:*` checks run.      |
| `SENDO_CONNECT_BASE_URL`                                | Optional. Default https://connect.sendo.dev.                                             |

> **Note:**
>
> Values of `SENDO_META_APP_SECRET`, `SENDO_VERIFY_TOKEN`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` and every resolved token, plus any env var whose name contains TOKEN, SECRET, KEY or PASSWORD, are scrubbed from the output.

## doctor

```shell
npx @quami/sendo doctor
npx @quami/sendo doctor --account 123456789012345        # one account (id or phone_number_id)
npx @quami/sendo doctor --url https://<app>/api/sendo/webhook # also test the webhook challenge
npx @quami/sendo doctor --json                           # machine-readable results
```

Prints a pass/fail table with a fix hint under each failure. Checks never throw: a broken step is reported and the rest still run. Each failure line is `FAIL`, followed by `-> Fix:` and a docs link. Warnings (`WARN`, `warning: true` in `--json`) carry a fix too but don't change the exit code.

## doctor checks

| id                                                   | Passes when                                                                                                                                                                  | Typical fix                                                                                                                                |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `env`                                                | SENDO_META_APP_SECRET, SENDO_VERIFY_TOKEN, Supabase URL + service role key and every account's token_ref are set.                                                            | Add them to .env.local / the deployment.                                                                                                   |
| `tables`                                             | All sendo\_\* tables exist.                                                                                                                                                  | Apply the schema migration.                                                                                                                |
| `schema-version`                                     | sendo_schema_meta matches the package (SENDO_SCHEMA_VERSION).                                                                                                                | Apply the latest migration.                                                                                                                |
| `storage`                                            | The SENDO_STORAGE_BUCKET bucket exists.                                                                                                                                      | Create a private bucket.                                                                                                                   |
| `accounts`                                           | At least one active sendo_accounts row.                                                                                                                                      | npx @quami/sendo accounts add                                                                                                              |
| `account:<phone_number_id>:token`                    | Reported (failing) only when the token env var is empty.                                                                                                                     | Set the variable named by token_ref.                                                                                                       |
| `account:<phone_number_id>:phone`                    | `GET /{phone_number_id}` works with the token; shows verification status and quality rating. RED quality fails.                                                              | Token expired (190) or wrong phone_number_id.                                                                                              |
| `account:<phone_number_id>:subscription`             | `GET /{waba_id}/subscribed_apps` lists at least one app (and SENDO_META_APP_ID, if set).                                                                                     | `POST /{waba_id}/subscribed_apps`; subscribe the messages field.                                                                           |
| `account:<phone_number_id>:templates`                | Templates can be listed from Meta (counts approved ones).                                                                                                                    | Token needs whatsapp_business_management.                                                                                                  |
| `account:<phone_number_id>:billing`                  | The stored `billingReady` is `true`. `false` or unknown (`null`) is a **warning**, not a failure.                                                                            | Add a payment method in Meta Business Settings, then `sendo.accounts.refreshBilling(id)` ([Billing state](https://sendo.dev/docs/embedded-signup#billing)). |
| `webhook-url`                                        | Only with --url: the GET verify challenge echoes the challenge with SENDO_VERIFY_TOKEN.                                                                                      | Deploy the route, align SENDO_VERIFY_TOKEN.                                                                                                |
| `connect:key`, `connect:webhook`, `connect:delivery` | Only with the Connect env vars: Connect accepts the key, has your webhook URL registered (equal to --url, if given) and its last delivery got a 2xx (none yet is a warning). | See [Sendo Connect](https://sendo.dev/docs/sendo-connect#doctor).                                                                                           |

The template check lists templates from Meta; it doesn’t write `sendo_templates`. Your app populates that table with `sendo.templates.sync()`.

## accounts add

```shell
# interactive (prompts for anything missing)
npx @quami/sendo accounts add

# non-interactive
npx @quami/sendo accounts add --phone-number-id 123456789012345 --token-env SENDO_TOKEN_MAIN \
  --waba-id 987654321098765 --tenant-id <uuid> --display-phone "+502 5555 1234" \
  --timezone America/Guatemala --yes
```

| Flag                | Notes                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--phone-number-id` | Required. Meta Phone number ID.                                                                                       |
| `--token-env`       | Required. Name of the env var with the token; it must be set and non-empty, or the command stops before calling Meta. |
| `--waba-id`         | Optional. Looked up from the token's debug_token scopes when there's a single candidate; otherwise asked for.         |
| `--display-phone`   | Optional. Fetched from Meta by default.                                                                               |
| `--tenant-id`       | Optional uuid. Default: no tenant (null).                                                                             |
| `--timezone`        | Optional IANA zone. Default America/Guatemala.                                                                        |
| `--yes, -y`         | No prompts; fail if a required value is missing. Prompts only happen on a TTY.                                        |

It inserts the row through the Supabase adapter and stores only the env var name in `token_ref`. An existing `phone_number_id` fails with `DuplicateAccountError`. To change a row later, use the commands below or [`sendo.accounts`](https://sendo.dev/docs/numbers-and-tenants#accounts).

## accounts list, set-default, disconnect

```shell
npx @quami/sendo accounts list                       # every number, connected or not
npx @quami/sendo accounts list --tenant-id <uuid> --json
npx @quami/sendo accounts set-default 123456789012345 # id or phone_number_id
npx @quami/sendo accounts disconnect 123456789012345
```

- `list` prints id, number, label, tenant, status (connected / disconnected), whether it is the tenant’s default and how it was onboarded. `--json` prints the `Account` objects.
- `set-default` makes the number its tenant’s default (atomic swap). A disconnected number exits 1.
- `disconnect` does what [`sendo.accounts.disconnect`](https://sendo.dev/docs/numbers-and-tenants#disconnect) does, except that the CLI has no `deleteToken` hook: it reminds you to delete the token yourself. For Embedded Signup numbers it unsubscribes the app from the WABA with the token in the env var named by `token_ref`, when it is set.

## rules sync

Stores the rules you declare in code in `sendo_rules`, where the rules screen and the engine read them.

```shell
npx @quami/sendo rules sync --config lib/sendo-rules.ts --tenant <uuid>
npx @quami/sendo rules sync --config lib/sendo-rules.ts --tenant <uuid> --force
```

- `--config` loads a JS or TS module (through `jiti`, CLI only) that exports `rules: RuleDefinition[]`. Keep the rules in a standalone file such as `lib/sendo-rules.ts` and import it from `lib/sendo.ts` too, so the CLI never loads Next.js-only code.
- Every rule is validated with the package's zod schemas first; one invalid rule exits 1 and nothing is written.
- Rules are inserted by `(tenant, key)` with origin `code`. A rule that already exists (for example, edited on the rules screen) is left as is unless you pass `--force`, which replaces its type, params and account; its position and on/off state stay as the screen left them.
- `--tenant` is the tenant of rules that don't declare `tenant`; rules declaring another tenant are skipped. A rule's `account` may be the sendo account id or the phone number id.

## mcp

`sendo mcp` runs a stdio MCP server for coding agents (docs search, API reference, registry items with their `AGENTS.md`, read-only doctor). You don't run it by hand: register `npx -y @quami/sendo mcp` in Claude Code or Cursor, see [Para agentes](https://sendo.dev/docs/agents-docs#setup).

`--config <path>` (doctor and mcp) loads a JS or TS module that exports `adapter`, for apps whose storage isn't the Supabase adapter built from env (see [run_doctor and your adapter](https://sendo.dev/docs/agents-docs#doctor)).

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning                                                                  |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 0    | Every check passed / the accounts or rules command worked.               |
| 1    | At least one check failed (warnings don't count), or the command failed. |
| 2    | Usage error (unknown command or flag).                                   |

## Programmatic use

`runDoctor`, `doctorExitCode`, `addAccount` and `findWabaIdsForToken` are exported from `@quami/sendo`:

```ts title="ts"
import { createGraphClient, doctorExitCode, runDoctor } from "@quami/sendo";
import { memoryAdapter } from "@quami/sendo/adapters/memory";

// The CLI is a thin wrapper: run the same checks from a test or a health endpoint.
const results = await runDoctor({
  env: process.env,
  adapter: memoryAdapter(), // or supabaseAdapter(...); null when it can't be built
  graph: createGraphClient(),
  url: "https://example.com/api/sendo/webhook",
});
for (const { id, ok, detail, hint } of results) {
  console.log(ok ? "✓" : "✗", id, detail, hint ?? "");
}
process.exitCode = doctorExitCode(results); // 0 or 1
```

- Each result is `{ id, label, ok, detail, fix?, hint?, warning? }`; `detail`, `fix` and `hint` never contain secrets. `warning: true` marks a failing check that doesn't fail the run.
- Setup walkthrough: [Quickstart step 8](https://sendo.dev/docs/quickstart#doctor).

docs.title: Voice notes and cost
docs.description: Transcribe inbound voice notes before the agent answers, and see what every agent turn and conversation cost.
docs.body:
Contacts send voice notes all the time. With one config option Sendo transcribes them before the agent turn, so the agent answers what was said and the inbox shows the transcript under the audio. Every agent turn also records its tokens and cost, which admins see in the inbox and in [Metrics](https://sendo.dev/docs/metrics).

## Voice notes

Pass any [AI SDK transcription model](https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/ai-sdk-core/transcription) as `transcribe.model`:

```ts title="lib/sendo.ts"
const sendo = createSendo({
  adapter: memoryAdapter(),
  appSecret: process.env.SENDO_META_APP_SECRET ?? "",
  verifyToken: process.env.SENDO_VERIFY_TOKEN ?? "",
  resolveToken: (account) => process.env[account.tokenRef],
  // Inbound voice notes are transcribed after the download and before the agent turn.
  transcribe: { model: whisper },
});
```

For each inbound `audio` message, the webhook pipeline:

1. downloads the audio into your media store (as for any media);
2. sends the bytes to the model with `experimental_transcribe` from `ai`, waiting at most 30 seconds;
3. stores the transcript as the message `text`, with `metadata.transcription = { model, ms }`;
4. then runs the opt-out check, the rules, the `message` event and the agent turn, which all see the transcript.

The agent reads a transcribed note as `[voice note] <transcript>`. Rules that match keywords match the transcript too.

`transcribe.timeoutMs` lowers the 30-second limit (1–30000). Without `transcribe`, nothing is sent to a model and the agent reads untranscribed voice notes as “[untranscribed voice note]”.

### When there is no transcript

Transcription never fails the webhook or the agent turn. When it doesn't produce text, `text` stays `null`, the agent reads “[untranscribed voice note]” and `metadata.transcription.error` says why:

| `error`     | What happened                                                               |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `too_large` | The note is over 25 MB (the usual provider limit); the model is not called. |
| `timeout`   | The model didn't answer within the time limit; the call is aborted.         |
| `no_audio`  | The audio couldn't be downloaded or read from the media store.              |
| `empty`     | The model returned no text.                                                 |
| `failed`    | The model threw (provider error, bad key…); the error is logged.            |

In the inbox the operator sees the audio player with the transcript below it, or a “Sin transcripción” label whose tooltip gives the reason. `sendo.inbox.thread` exposes the same record as `transcription: { model, ms, error } | null` on each message (`null` when no transcription was attempted).

> **Note:**
>
> Transcription bills your speech-to-text provider per audio minute. It runs for every inbound voice note, including those of conversations handled by a person, so the team can read them too.

## Cost per agent turn

Each agent reply or draft stores `tokensIn`, `tokensOut` and `costCents` (US cents). The cost comes from the provider’s reported cost when available (for example OpenRouter), otherwise from the agent’s `pricing` (`{ inputPerMTok, outputPerMTok }` in USD), otherwise it is `null`. Details in [Agents and models](https://sendo.dev/docs/agents-and-models#cost).

Only admins (`costs.view`) see cost and tokens; for everyone else `sendo.inbox.thread` returns them as `null`.

## Cost in the inbox

- **Per turn:** hovering an agent reply shows its cost and tokens (`$0.0024 · 1102 → 64 tokens`), or “—” when the cost is unknown. On touch screens the line is always visible. Other roles never see it.
- **Per conversation:** the context panel’s “Costo del agente” shows the number of agent turns and their total cost for the whole conversation, plus how many turns have no known cost.

The total comes from `sendo.inbox.cost`, which the inbox `thread` action calls for admins:

```ts title="ts"
// Admins only (`costs.view`); everyone else gets FORBIDDEN.
const actor: Actor = await sendo.actor(userId, tenantId);
const cost = await sendo.inbox.cost(conversationId, { actor });
// { turns: 12, tokensIn: 13_480, tokensOut: 702, costCents: 2.71, unpricedTurns: 0 }
console.log(cost);
```

`turns` counts agent replies and pending drafts (the model ran for both). `costCents` is `null` when no turn has a known cost. Cost per day and per agent across conversations is in [Metrics](https://sendo.dev/docs/metrics).
