docs.title: Para agentes
docs.description: Docs for coding agents: the sendo mcp server (one-line setup for Claude Code and Cursor), llms.txt, AGENTS.md in every registry item and doctor --json.
docs.body:
Sendo is built so a coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, …) never has to guess the API. Four sources, all generated from the same code and docs:

| Source                                                                                    | What it gives the agent                                                                                                                          |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `sendo mcp`                                                                               | An MCP server inside the installed package: docs search, exact signatures, registry items, doctor. Always matches the version in `node_modules`. |
| [llms.txt](https://sendo.dev/llms.txt) · [llms-full.txt](https://sendo.dev/llms-full.txt) | The docs index, and every page as Markdown with the code samples inlined (latest release).                                                       |
| `components/sendo/<item>/AGENTS.md`                                                       | Installed with each registry item: what it is, files safe to edit, what not to touch and why, how it connects, how to verify it.                 |
| `npx @quami/sendo doctor --json`                                                          | Every setup check as JSON; each failing check has `fix: { kind, detail, docsUrl }`.                                                              |

## Setup

Run it from your app's root, where `@quami/sendo` is installed.

**Claude Code** (writes `.mcp.json`, so the whole team gets it):

```shell
claude mcp add --transport stdio --scope project sendo -- npx -y @quami/sendo mcp
```

**Cursor**: add this to `.cursor/mcp.json` (or `~/.cursor/mcp.json` for every project):

```json title=".cursor/mcp.json"
{ "mcpServers": { "sendo": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@quami/sendo", "mcp"] } } }
```

Or open the install link `cursor://anysphere.cursor-deeplink/mcp/install?name=sendo&config=eyJjb21tYW5kIjoibnB4IiwiYXJncyI6WyIteSIsIkBxdWFtaS9zZW5kbyIsIm1jcCJdfQ==` in Cursor.

Any other MCP client: command `npx`, args `-y @quami/sendo mcp`, transport stdio. The server writes nothing but protocol messages to stdout and exits when the client closes it.

## Tools

| Tool                  | Input                | Returns                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------------- | -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `search_docs`         | `{ query, limit? }`  | BM25 search over every docs page, by section: title, URL, a `read_doc` reference (`slug#anchor`) and a snippet.                                                                                     |
| `read_doc`            | `{ slug }`           | One page as Markdown (`quickstart`), or one section (`cli#checks`).                                                                                                                                 |
| `api_reference`       | `{ symbol }`         | Declaration, JSDoc and import path of any export of `@quami/sendo` and its subpaths. Accepts `createSendo`, `InboxApi.reply` and instance paths like `sendo.inbox.reply`. Typos get "Did you mean". |
| `list_registry_items` | none                 | Every `@sendo/*` item with its description, install command and where its `AGENTS.md` lands.                                                                                                        |
| `get_registry_item`   | `{ name }`           | Files and install targets, dependencies, env vars, post-install notes and the item's `AGENTS.md`.                                                                                                   |
| `run_doctor`          | `{ account?, url? }` | Same JSON as `sendo doctor --json`, for the app in the working directory. Read-only.                                                                                                                |

All tools are read-only. Secrets from the environment are scrubbed from every response.

## Where the data comes from

- **Docs:** `docs/docs.json` in the package, generated from these MDX pages (`pnpm --filter web build:llms`), the same source as `llms.txt`.
- **API reference:** `dist/api.json`, generated at package build from the published `.d.ts` files, so it is exactly the API you have installed.
- **Registry:** `dist/registry.json`, the registry manifest plus every item's `AGENTS.md`, also generated at build.

## run_doctor and your adapter

`run_doctor` (like `sendo doctor`) loads `.env.development.local`, `.env.local` and `.env` from the working directory and builds the Supabase adapter from `SUPABASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`. If your app uses another adapter (Drizzle, Prisma, your own), export it from a module without Next.js imports and pass it with `--config`:

```ts title="lib/sendo-adapter.ts"
import { supabaseAdapter } from "@quami/sendo/adapters/supabase";
import { createClient } from "@supabase/supabase-js";

// Or your Drizzle / Prisma / custom SendoAdapter. Relative imports only: no `@/` aliases.
export const adapter = supabaseAdapter(
  createClient(process.env.SUPABASE_URL!, process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY!),
);
```

```shell
claude mcp add --transport stdio --scope project sendo -- npx -y @quami/sendo mcp --config lib/sendo-adapter.ts
npx @quami/sendo doctor --config lib/sendo-adapter.ts
```

## AGENTS.md in every item

Every registry item ships an `AGENTS.md` (installed at `components/sendo/<item>/AGENTS.md`) with the same sections: an intro saying what the item is, **Files** (which ones are yours to edit), **Don't touch** (what lives in npm and why), **Connects to** (env vars, `createSendo` hooks, database hooks, other items) and **Verify** (how to check it works). Items with UI also ship `MOTION.md` next to it. `get_registry_item` returns the same text before you install anything.

docs.title: Migrating from Respond.io or Kapso
docs.description: Move a WhatsApp number, contacts and workflows from a hosted inbox into your own app with Sendo.

headings.title: 1. Install Sendo next to the old tool

docs.body:
Respond.io and Kapso are hosted inboxes. Sendo does the same job inside your app: the conversations land in your database and the inbox is a screen of your product. Migrating is mostly about the WhatsApp number, because everything else is yours to import.

> **Note: Plan the cut-over**
>
> A WhatsApp number can only be connected to one Cloud API app at a time. Expect a short window in which messages go to neither tool, and do it when your traffic is low.

## Concepts

| Respond.io / Kapso                     | Sendo                                                                              |
| -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Workspace / project                    | Your app; organizations are `tenantId`                                             |
| Channel (WhatsApp number)              | `sendo_accounts` row ([Numbers and tenants](https://sendo.dev/docs/numbers-and-tenants))            |
| Contact                                | `sendo_contacts`, linked to your own record through `linkContact` / `appRef`       |
| Inbox, assignment, notes               | `inbox` and `sendo.inbox` ([Team inbox](https://sendo.dev/docs/team-inbox))                         |
| Users and roles                        | Your users; Sendo asks `resolveRole`, `resolveUsers`, `resolveAssignees`           |
| Saved replies, tags                    | Snippets and tags                                                                  |
| Workflows, business hours, auto-assign | Rules ([Workflows](https://sendo.dev/docs/workflows)); anything else is your code (`sendo.on(...)`) |
| AI agent                               | `sendo.agent({...})` with any model ([Agents and models](https://sendo.dev/docs/agents-and-models)) |
| Broadcasts                             | `sendo.broadcasts` ([Broadcasts](https://sendo.dev/docs/broadcasts))                                |
| Reports                                | `sendo.metrics` and the Métricas screen ([Metrics](https://sendo.dev/docs/metrics))                 |

## 1. Install Sendo next to the old tool

Follow the [quickstart](https://sendo.dev/docs/quickstart) with a **test number** first, so the webhook, the agent and the inbox are proven before you touch the real number.

## 2. Move the number

- **If you own the Meta app and the WhatsApp Business account** (you created them, or the old tool connected through your own app): point the app’s webhook at `https://<your-app>/api/sendo/webhook`, add the number with `npx @quami/sendo accounts add`, and run `npx @quami/sendo doctor`. Your templates stay, because they belong to the WhatsApp Business account.
- **If the old tool is the Meta Tech Provider or BSP**: disconnect the number there, then connect it to your app through [Embedded Signup](https://sendo.dev/docs/embedded-signup) or Meta’s phone number migration flow. Templates belong to the old WhatsApp Business account; if the number moves to a new one, re-submit them and wait for approval before you need them.

Check Meta’s current documentation for number migration before you start; the steps depend on who owns the business account.

## 3. Import contacts and consent

Export contacts from the old tool (CSV) and upsert them with the adapter or your own SQL (`sendo_contacts`: account, phone, profile name). Bring marketing consent along: record it with `sendo.contacts.setOptIn(contactId, true, { source: "import" })`, because [broadcasts](https://sendo.dev/docs/broadcasts) of MARKETING templates only go to contacts who opted in.

## 4. Conversation history

Sendo doesn’t import another tool’s message history. Keep the export as an archive, or insert it yourself with the adapter if your team needs it in the thread. New conversations start in Sendo from the cut-over.

## 5. Rebuild workflows as rules

Business hours, routing by keyword, auto-assign, escalation and auto-close are [rules](https://sendo.dev/docs/workflows), editable on the Reglas screen or kept in code with `sendo rules sync`. Anything more specific is a few lines of your own code on Sendo events.

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.description: What already shipped, what Sendo Connect is and isn’t, when it opens, and the channels still to come.
docs.body:
Sendo is a library. Your messages, contacts and media live only in your own database, and that doesn’t change on this page.

## Shipped

These items were on the V2 plan and are now part of `@quami/sendo` and the registry:

- **Embedded Signup**: `sendo.accounts.completeEmbeddedSignup` and the `numbers` item ([Embedded Signup](https://sendo.dev/docs/embedded-signup)).
- **Broadcasts and opt-in**: `sendo.broadcasts`, `sendo.contacts.setOptIn` and the `broadcasts` item ([Broadcasts](https://sendo.dev/docs/broadcasts)).
- **Metrics**: SQL views, `sendo.metrics` and the `metrics` item ([Metrics](https://sendo.dev/docs/metrics)).
- **Drizzle and Prisma adapters**: `@quami/sendo/adapters/drizzle` and `@quami/sendo/adapters/prisma`, both passing `runAdapterContract` ([Adapters](https://sendo.dev/docs/adapters)).
- **Voice notes and cost**: the `transcribe` option and per-turn cost ([Voice notes and cost](https://sendo.dev/docs/voice-notes-and-cost)).
- **Sendo Connect (package side)**: the `connect` option, signup through Connect and the doctor checks ([Sendo Connect](https://sendo.dev/docs/sendo-connect)).

## Sendo Connect

Connect is the only paid piece. Quami acts as the Meta **Tech Provider** for your app, so you can offer “Connect your WhatsApp” without going through Meta’s business verification and app review yourself.

### What it is

- **A signed webhook relay.** Meta sends webhooks for your numbers to Quami’s relay, which signs each one with your own secret (`X-Sendo-Signature`) and posts it to your app. Your app verifies it and fails closed.
- **A signup API.** It completes Embedded Signup with Quami’s Meta app and returns the number’s token to your server once.
- **A minimal panel.** API key, signing secret, your webhook URL, connected numbers and their billing status.
- **Per-number billing.** Connect bills per connected number, per month ([Pricing](https://sendo.dev/pricing)). Meta still bills messages to your customer’s WhatsApp Business account.

### What it isn’t

- **Not an inbox.** The inbox is the `inbox` item in your app, reading your database.
- **Not a message store.** Connect keeps no copy of your messages, contacts or media.
- **Not user management.** Your staff, roles and tenants stay in your app.
- **Not a sending proxy.** Your server sends straight to Meta with the token Connect returned at signup. Connect never sends on your behalf and doesn’t keep that token.

It’s a piece, not a platform. Adding `connect` to `createSendo` is a configuration change; the package, the migrations and the registry items stay the same.

### The privacy cost

With Connect, your customers’ webhooks **pass through Quami** before they reach you. That is a third party in the path of every inbound message:

- A webhook body is held encrypted only while its delivery is pending, and deleted on success or when the 24-hour retry window ends.
- Bodies are never logged. Only delivery metadata (timestamp, project, number, status code, attempt count, latency) is kept, for 7 days.
- Quami’s Meta app is the one connected to your customers’ WhatsApp accounts.

If that cost is too high for your data (health, for example), use your own Meta app. Doing Meta’s paperwork yourself stays free and first-class: see [Meta setup](https://sendo.dev/docs/meta-setup) and [Embedded Signup](https://sendo.dev/docs/embedded-signup).

### When it ships

The package side already ships in `@quami/sendo`. Connect accounts open after Meta approves Quami as a Tech Provider; there is no date until that approval arrives. Until then, use [your own Meta app](https://sendo.dev/docs/meta-setup).

## Planned

> **Warning: Not available**
>
> Everything below is planned. None of it ships yet, there are no dates, and the names may change.

### More channels

WhatsApp is the only channel today. Instagram and Messenger come next: the schema, the webhook dispatch and the inbox already carry a `channel`, so a new channel is new code in the package, not a migration in your app ([Channels](https://sendo.dev/docs/channels)). The `Transport` interface stays swappable for the same reason, so a new channel or a new way to reach Meta doesn’t mean rewriting your app ([Transport](https://sendo.dev/docs/api-reference#transport)).

### diff CLI

`npx @quami/sendo diff` fetches the latest registry items and compares them with your installed files and `sendo_schema_meta.version`, with a changelog. Until then the package warns at startup when the installed schema is older than it expects.
